lines.text: Footprints in the snow led to the farm. None led away.
Bavaria, March 1922. A lonely farm called Hinterkaifeck.
The farmer, Andreas Gruber, reportedly told neighbours about the tracks.
He'd heard footsteps in the attic. He searched. Nobody.
A Munich newspaper turned up that nobody had bought.
Then a house key went missing.
Their previous maid had already quit. She'd heard noises in the attic too.
On March thirty-first, the new maid arrived. Her first day.
That night, all six people on the farm were killed.
No one found them for four days.
And that's where it gets stranger.
Neighbours later said smoke rose from the chimney in those days.
Someone had been feeding the cattle.
Investigators concluded the killer stayed on the farm for days.
Police looked at more than a hundred suspects. Nobody was ever convicted.
In 2007, police students re-examined the files with modern methods.
They reportedly narrowed it to one main suspect, but never named that person publicly.
Officially, the case is still unsolved.
Why would anyone stay? Tell me what you think.
And it all began in the snow.
